title: Countable structure spaces, Part II: Borel reducibility of isomorphism relations and Borel completeness
summary: Compares isomorphism relations of classes of countable structures by Borel reducibility; defines Borel completeness (also for languages with function symbols); proves by explicit continuous codings that graphs, linear orders and trees are Borel complete (Friedman–Stanley); embeds every Borel S∞-space into the logic action of the language with one n-ary symbol per n (Becker–Kechris for S∞, through the Polish realization of NoncompactQuantumSymmetry); proves the characterisations of Borel completeness; and shows that a Borel complete isomorphism relation is not Borel, lies above E₀, has continuum many classes and unbounded Scott height, with the Friedman–Stanley obstruction lemma.

layers.title: Isomorphism relations of classes and two reducibilities

targets.name: classIso
targets.statement: For any carrier α and K : Set (RelationalConfiguration L α), classIso K : Setoid K := Setoid.comap Subtype.val (isoSetoid L α), the pullback of Tau Ceti's isoSetoid L α along the inclusion K → RelationalConfiguration L α; K carries the subtype σ-algebra. BorelComplete (1.2) uses it on ℕ; relabelling (1.1) uses it on arbitrary carriers.
hypotheses: L is a relational first-order language ([L.IsRelational]) (no countability needed for the definition)
α : Type w an arbitrary carrier (finite, empty or infinite)

locator.where: Definition 1.4, line 83; camerlo-gao-boolean lines 106–110 for classes

api.name: classIso_iff
api.statement: For x y : K, classIso K x y holds iff the decoded structures of x and y are isomorphic (isoSetoid_apply), iff x and y lie in one orbit of the logic action of Equiv.Perm α (isoSetoid_eq_orbitRel).

api.name: borelReducible_classIso_univ
api.statement: On every carrier α, classIso (Set.univ : Set (RelationalConfiguration L α)) and isoSetoid L α are Borel reducible to each other, the inclusion of univ being a measurable equivalence.

api.name: quotient_injection
api.statement: A Borel reduction of classIso K' to classIso K induces an injection of quotients (Tau Ceti BorelReducible.exists_measurable_injective_quotient, not restated); it need not be injective on codes.

tests.name: two_orbit_class
tests.statement: In the language of one unary predicate, the class {P = ∅, P = ℕ} is invariant Borel and classIso of it is equality with exactly two classes; the class 'P finite' has one class per finite size.

tests.name: empty_class
tests.statement: classIso ∅ reduces to every classIso K by the empty map, and classIso K reduces to classIso ∅ iff K = ∅.

tests.name: noninjective_reduction
tests.statement: For K' the codes with P infinite and coinfinite (one orbit, uncountably many codes) and any nonempty K, the constant map reduces classIso K' to classIso K without being injective on codes.

tests.name: noninvariant_subclass
tests.statement: For A the single code P = {0} inside the class |P| = 1, the inclusion reduces classIso A to classIso K; both have one class.

tests.name: finite_carrier
tests.statement: On the carrier Fin 2 with one unary predicate, classIso univ has three classes on four codes (|P| = 0, 1, 2): P = {0} and P = {1} are related (not equality on codes), P = ∅ and P = {0} are not (not the trivial relation).

targets.name: borelReducible_classIso_of_subset
targets.statement: For sets A ⊆ K of codes on one carrier α, classIso A is Borel reducible to classIso K; hence if classIso K' is Borel reducible to classIso K and A ⊆ K', then classIso A is Borel reducible to classIso K. Route: classIso A is Setoid.comap of classIso K along the measurable inclusion A → K, and Tau Ceti's Setoid.borelReducible_comap applies.
hypotheses: L is a relational first-order language ([L.IsRelational])
A, K, K' arbitrary sets of codes of relational languages on arbitrary carriers (no Borelness needed); the two sides of each inclusion are codes of one language on one carrier

tests.name: restriction_to_orbit
tests.statement: Restricting the reduction of 2.5 to the orbit of one code of RelationalConfiguration L' ℕ gives a reduction of a one-class relation.

targets.name: borelReducible_classIso_of_measurable
targets.statement: For carriers β and α, if f : RelationalConfiguration L' β → RelationalConfiguration L α is measurable, maps K' : Set (RelationalConfiguration L' β) into K : Set (RelationalConfiguration L α), and for all x y ∈ K' the codes x, y are isomorphic iff f x, f y are, then classIso K' is Borel reducible to classIso K. Route: the corestriction K' → K of f is measurable and Tau Ceti's Setoid.borelReducible_iff_exists_eq_comap applies.
hypotheses: L is a relational first-order language ([L.IsRelational]) (no countability needed)

targets.name: SetReducible
targets.statement: SetReducible A B for A : Set X, B : Set Y on measurable spaces: ∃ f : X → Y measurable with ∀ x, x ∈ A ↔ f x ∈ B.

api.name: SetReducible.refl/trans
api.statement: SetReducible is reflexive and transitive.

api.name: setReducible_compl_iff
api.statement: SetReducible A B ↔ SetReducible Aᶜ Bᶜ.

api.name: SetReducible.measurableSet
api.statement: SetReducible A B and MeasurableSet B give MeasurableSet A.

api.name: SetReducible.analyticSet
api.statement: For X, Y Polish with Borel σ-algebras, SetReducible A B and AnalyticSet B give AnalyticSet A (refine the topology by Measurable.exists_continuous, then AnalyticSet.preimage).

api.name: setReducible_empty_iff
api.statement: SetReducible A (∅ : Set Y) ↔ A = ∅ ∧ (IsEmpty X ∨ Nonempty Y): the right side records that some map X → Y exists (the empty map, or a constant map, both measurable).

api.name: setReducible_univ_iff
api.statement: SetReducible A (Set.univ : Set Y) ↔ A = Set.univ ∧ (IsEmpty X ∨ Nonempty Y).

tests.name: singleton_to_diagonal
tests.statement: A = {0} ⊆ ℕ, B the diagonal of Cantor space squared: the map 0 ↦ (0,0), n+1 ↦ (0,1) has preimage {0}.

tests.name: empty_and_univ_targets
tests.statement: Negative control for the existence clause: X = Unit, Y = Empty, A = ∅ satisfies A = ∅, yet no map Unit → Empty exists, so A is not set reducible to ∅ ⊆ Empty, and A = Set.univ ⊆ Unit is not set reducible to Set.univ ⊆ Empty; for X = Y = Empty the empty map witnesses both; for nonempty Y, A is set reducible to ∅ iff A = ∅ and to Set.univ iff A = Set.univ.

tests.name: nonborel_not_reducible
tests.statement: The complement of the base's wellOrderClass is analytic and not Borel, so it is not set reducible to the (Borel) diagonal.

tests.name: equality_pullback
tests.statement: For injective measurable f, the graph of equality on X is the preimage of the diagonal of Y under Prod.map f f.

targets.name: setReducible_graph_of_borelReducible
targets.statement: If BorelReducible E F for setoids E on X and F on Y, then {p | E p.1 p.2} is SetReducible to {p | F p.1 p.2}, by Prod.map f f.

targets.name: setReducible_eZero_diagonal
targets.statement: The graph of TauCeti.eZero is SetReducible to the diagonal of (ℕ → Bool) × (ℕ → Bool) (it is Borel, measurableSet_eZero), whereas eZero is not Setoid.BorelReducible to (⊥ : Setoid (ℕ → Bool)) (that is Setoid.IsSmooth eZero, refuted by not_isSmooth_eZero); so set reducibility of graphs does not imply Borel reducibility.

targets.name: relabelHomeomorph
targets.statement: For any language L and e : α ≃ β, relabelling along e is Tau Ceti's RelationalConfiguration.restrict e.symm : RelationalConfiguration L α → RelationalConfiguration L β (value c.eval (atom R (e.symm ∘ w)) at atom R w). Bundle it as a homeomorphism and measurable equivalence with inverse restrict e. The library has the unbundled map with restrict_id, restrict_comp, measurable_restrict and continuous_restrict, and identifies relabelling with transport of the decoded structure only for permutations (perm_smul_eq_encodeVia); the bundled equivalence and the identification for an arbitrary bijection are new.
hypotheses: any language L (relational, [L.IsRelational], for the decoding, isomorphism and classIso statements)
e : α ≃ β for arbitrary carriers α, β

locator.where: lines 159–164 (the logic action as relabelling of structures on ℕ)

api.name: relabelHomeomorph_trans/relabelHomeomorph_refl
api.statement: Relabelling along e.trans e' is the composite and along Equiv.refl is the identity; the inverse is relabelling along e.symm (restrict_comp, restrict_id).

api.name: relabelHomeomorph_perm
api.statement: For α = β = ℕ, relabelling along σ is the logic action σ • · (perm_smul_def).

api.name: relabelHomeomorph_eq_encodeVia
api.statement: For relational L, the relabelled code is @Equiv.encodeVia L α β c.toStructure e (both read c.eval (atom R (e.symm ∘ w)) at atom R w, by eval_restrict and eval_encodeVia); c and its relabelling decode to isomorphic structures (Equiv.nonempty_equiv_encodeVia).

api.name: relabelHomeomorph_iso_iff
api.statement: For relational L, two codes on α are isomorphic iff their relabellings are (Equiv.isoSetoid_encodeVia_iff). For any K : Set (RelationalConfiguration L α) with image K₂ : Set (RelationalConfiguration L β): K invariant Borel implies K₂ invariant Borel; classIso K and classIso K₂ (0.1 on the carriers α and β) are Borel reducible to each other, by the corestriction law 0.3 applied to relabelling along e and along e.symm, which restrict to mutually inverse measurable bijections K ≃ K₂.

tests.name: transposition
tests.statement: Relabelling P = {0} along the transposition (0 1) gives P = {1}, equal to the logic action.

tests.name: fin_zero
tests.statement: On Fin 0 the coding space of a language without nullary symbols is one point and relabelling is the identity; with one nullary symbol, two fixed points. For K the whole coding space on Fin 0, classIso K has one class, respectively two (the nullary symbol separates the two codes), and the identity reduces it to itself both ways.

tests.name: fin_three_direction
tests.statement: One unary predicate on Fin 3, e the 3-cycle 0 ↦ 1 ↦ 2 ↦ 0: the class {P = {0}} relabels to {P = {1}} (new predicate e(P)); the reverse convention restrict e would give {P = {2}}. Both have one classIso class. The class of all eight codes is invariant, its own image, and classIso of it has four classes (|P| = 0, 1, 2, 3), each mapped onto itself.

tests.name: three_cycle_twice
tests.statement: Relabelling P = {0} twice along the 3-cycle 0→1→2→0 gives P = {2} ≠ {0}, while relabelling along e then e.symm is the identity.

targets.name: BorelComplete
targets.statement: BorelComplete K for K : Set (RelationalConfiguration L ℕ): for every L' : Language.{0,0} with [L'.IsRelational] [∀ n, Countable (L'.Relations n)] and every K' : Set (RelationalConfiguration L' ℕ) with MeasurableSet K' and IsomorphismInvariant K', Setoid.BorelReducible (classIso K') (classIso K).
hypotheses: L is a relational first-order language ([L.IsRelational]) with countably many relation symbols ([∀ n, Countable (L.Relations n)])

api.name: BorelComplete.of_borelReducible
api.statement: BorelComplete K and Setoid.BorelReducible (classIso K) (classIso K₂) give BorelComplete K₂; in particular K ⊆ K₂.

api.name: borelComplete_congr
api.statement: Borel completeness depends only on classIso K up to Borel bireducibility.

api.name: BorelComplete.borelReducible_univ
api.statement: If BorelComplete K then every invariant Borel class of a countable relational language in any universes reduces to K (target 1.3).

api.name: borelComplete_map_lequiv_iff
api.statement: For a language equivalence e : L ≃ᴸ L₂ of countable relational languages, K is Borel complete iff e.onConfiguration '' K is (Tau Ceti LEquiv.onConfiguration).

tests.name: empty_not_complete
tests.statement: BorelComplete ∅ fails: K' = univ for one unary symbol is nonempty.

tests.name: countably_many_types
tests.statement: The class of codes of one unary predicate is not Borel complete: the closed class of codes of countably many unary predicates each ∅ or ℕ has types in bijection with ℕ → Bool and cannot inject into a countable quotient.

tests.name: union_not_intersection
tests.statement: If K is Borel complete so is K ∪ K₂; graphClass ∩ (orbit of the empty graph) is one orbit and not Borel complete.

tests.name: renaming
tests.statement: Renaming adj in Language.graph gives an equivalent language and the image of graphClass is Borel complete.

targets.name: BorelComplete.borelReducible_univ
targets.statement: If BorelComplete K, then for every L' : Language.{u', v'} with [L'.IsRelational] [∀ n, Countable (L'.Relations n)] and every invariant Borel K' ⊆ RelationalConfiguration L' ℕ, classIso K' is Borel reducible to classIso K. Route: transport K' along Tau Ceti's smallPresentationEquiv L' by LEquiv.onConfiguration, a homeomorphism measurable both ways that preserves and reflects isomorphism (isoSetoid_onConfiguration_iff).
hypotheses: L is a relational first-order language ([L.IsRelational]) with countably many relation symbols ([∀ n, Countable (L.Relations n)])
L' countable relational in arbitrary universes

locator.where: lines 87–93 and 101–105 (Mod(L) for an arbitrary countable language)

targets.name: FunCode
targets.statement: For L with countably many function and relation symbols, the functional coding space: pairs (F, c) of a table F : (Σ f : (Σ l, L.Functions l), Fin f.1 → ℕ) → ℕ and a relation code c : RelationalConfiguration L ℕ, with the product topology; decoding to L.Structure ℕ; the action (σ • F)⟨f, v⟩ = σ (F ⟨f, σ⁻¹ ∘ v⟩) and the logic action on c.

locator.where: lines 60–64 (groups, abelian groups and torsion-free abelian groups as Borel subsets of the space of structures)

api.name: polishSpace_funCode
api.statement: The functional coding space is Polish and the action is continuous.

api.name: orbitRel_funCode_iff
api.statement: Two points lie in one orbit iff their decoded L-structures are isomorphic.

api.name: measurableSet_models
api.statement: The models on ℕ of a set of first-order L-sentences form an invariant Borel set (target 1.6).

api.name: funCode_relational
api.statement: For relational L the table is the empty map and the space is RelationalConfiguration L ℕ.

tests.name: constant_symbol
tests.statement: For one constant symbol k, a table is one number F k; the table F k = 3 decodes to the structure interpreting k as 3.

tests.name: no_symbols
tests.statement: For the empty language the functional coding space is a single point.

tests.name: orbit_of_constant
tests.statement: Two tables F k = 3 and F k = 5 are in one orbit (transposition (3 5)), while a table and a non-isomorphic relation code are not.

targets.name: graphCodeFun_homeomorph
targets.statement: The graph-code map from the functional coding space to RelationalConfiguration (graphLanguage L) ℕ, sending a point to the code (ofStructure) of Tau Ceti's graphExpansion L ℕ of its decoded structure, is continuous, injective and equivariant; its range is the Gδ set of codes whose graph relations are graphs of total functions, which is not closed when L has at least one function symbol and is the whole coding space when L is relational; it is a homeomorphism onto its range, agreeing there with Tau Ceti's reconstructStructure (reconstructStructure_graphExpansion), the range being the codes whose decoded structure models graphAxioms of all function symbols (model_graphAxioms_iff); and two points decode to isomorphic structures iff their graph codes are isomorphic.
hypotheses: L with countably many function and relation symbols

tests.name: constant_graph
tests.statement: For one constant symbol and F k = 3, the unary graph relation is {3}.

tests.name: not_in_range
tests.statement: A graph code whose unary-function relation holds at (0,1) and (0,2), or at no (0,y), is not in the range; codes with value n at 0 converge as n → ∞ to a code with no value at 0, so the range is not closed.

tests.name: relational_case
tests.statement: For relational L the map is Tau Ceti's LEquiv.onConfiguration along the language equivalence L ≃ᴸ graphLanguage L sending R to GraphRelation.base R (an equivalence since L has no function symbols), and its range is the whole coding space, which is closed.

targets.name: measurableSet_funCode_models
targets.statement: For a set T of first-order L-sentences, the set of points of the functional coding space whose decoded structure is a model of T is measurable and invariant.
hypotheses: L with countably many function and relation symbols

tests.name: simple_graphs
tests.statement: For Language.graph and Theory.simpleGraph the set is graphClass.

tests.name: fields_char_two
tests.statement: For Language.ring and Theory.fieldOfChar 2 the set contains a code of 𝔽₂(t) and no code of ℚ.

targets.name: BorelComplete.borelReducible_funCode
targets.statement: If K₀ ⊆ RelationalConfiguration L₀ ℕ is Borel complete, then for every L' with countably many function and relation symbols and every invariant Borel class K' of the functional coding space of L', the isomorphism relation of K' is Borel reducible to classIso K₀; an invariant Borel class K of a functional coding space is called Borel complete when its graph-code image is.

layers.title: Every countable structure codes into a graph

targets.name: incidenceGraph
targets.statement: For countable relational L' and an injection ι of its relation symbols into ℕ, the coloured graph H_c on points p_a (a ∈ ℕ), tuple vertices t_q, position vertices s_{q,j} (j < arity) and truth vertices u_q (q : Atom L' ℕ), coloured κ(p) = 0, κ(u) = 1, κ(s_{q,j}) = 2+2j, κ(t_{⟨R,v⟩}) = 3+2ι(R), with edges t_q—s_{q,j}, s_{q,j}—p_{v j}, and t_q—u_q iff c.eval q = true.
hypotheses: L' relational with countably many relation symbols

locator.where: Theorem VI.27, lines 4582–4594 (coding a structure by gadgets attached to tuples; different gadgets)

api.name: incidenceGraph_bipartite
api.statement: H_c is bipartite (points and tuple vertices against positions and truth vertices), hence triangle-free.

api.name: incidenceGraph_adj_continuous
api.statement: Only tuple–truth edges depend on c, each on one coordinate c q.

api.name: incidenceGraph_iso_iff
api.statement: c ≅ d iff some colour-preserving bijection of base vertices maps H_c onto H_d (target 2.2).

tests.name: one_binary_edge
tests.statement: For R = {(0,1)}: t_{⟨R,![0,1]⟩} has three neighbours, t_{⟨R,![1,0]⟩} two.

tests.name: empty_language
tests.statement: For L' with no relation symbols, H_c has only points and no edges.

tests.name: nullary_symbol
tests.statement: A nullary symbol gives a tuple vertex without position neighbours, joined to its truth vertex iff the code says true.

tests.name: colours_needed
tests.statement: With two unary symbols, the codes P₁ = {0} and P₂ = {0} are not isomorphic but have isomorphic uncoloured incidence graphs.

targets.name: incidenceGraph_iso_iff
targets.statement: For codes c, d ∈ RelationalConfiguration L' ℕ: c and d are isomorphic iff there is a colour-preserving graph isomorphism H_c ≅ H_d. Route: d = σ • c by eval_perm_smul, and isoSetoid_iff_exists_perm_smul_eq.

targets.name: cliqueTag
targets.statement: For a triangle-free simple graph H on V with κ : V → ℕ, the tagged graph on V ⊕ Σ x, Fin (κ x + 3): H, a clique on the tag vertices of each x, and an edge from x to its tag vertex 0. Two triangle-free coloured graphs have isomorphic tagged graphs iff they are colour-isomorphic.

locator.where: Theorem VI.27, lines 4623–4654 (flags distinguishing coded vertices)

api.name: mem_triangle_iff_tag
api.statement: A vertex lies in a triangle iff it is a tag vertex.

api.name: cliqueTag_adj_base
api.statement: Edges between non-tag vertices are those of H.

api.name: cliqueTag_colour
api.statement: For non-tag x, κ x + 2 is the number of triangle vertices adjacent to the unique triangle-vertex neighbour of x.

tests.name: single_edge
tests.statement: One edge {x,y} with κ = (0,1): 9 vertices and 12 edges.

tests.name: empty
tests.statement: V = ∅ gives the empty graph.

tests.name: triangle_breaks
tests.statement: In the tagged graph of a triangle the original vertices lie in triangles, so the recognition rule fails without triangle-freeness.

tests.name: colour_detected
tests.statement: The tagged one-vertex graphs with κ = 0 and κ = 1 have 4 and 5 vertices and are not isomorphic.

targets.name: graphClass
targets.statement: graphClass : Set (RelationalConfiguration Language.graph ℕ) := {c | IsSimpleGraph c}, Tau Ceti's simple-graph codes (adjacency symmetric and false on the diagonal); equivalently the decoded adj is irreflexive and symmetric, the models of Theory.simpleGraph (Theory.simpleGraph_model_iff). Its API is cited from Tau Ceti and the base, not restated.

api.name: isClosed_graphClass
api.statement: graphClass is measurable (Tau Ceti measurableSet_setOf_isSimpleGraph), closed (CountableStructureSpaces Layer 0, closedness of the range of the graph coding) and invariant (σ • c = c.restrict σ⁻¹ by perm_smul_def, and IsSimpleGraph.restrict).

api.name: range_toRelationalConfiguration
api.statement: graphClass is the range of SimpleGraph.toRelationalConfiguration (Tau Ceti SimpleGraph.range_toRelationalConfiguration, by definition of graphClass), and SimpleGraph.relationalConfigurationEquiv is a measurable equivalence between SimpleGraph ℕ and the subtype graphClass; as a Borel subset of a Polish space graphClass is standard Borel (Mathlib MeasurableSet.standardBorel).

api.name: mem_graphClass_iff
api.statement: c ∈ graphClass iff IsSimpleGraph c (isSimpleGraph_iff: the atoms adjAtom u v and adjAtom v u agree and adjAtom v v is false), iff the decoded adj is irreflexive and symmetric.

tests.name: empty_graph
tests.statement: The code of the empty graph is in graphClass.

tests.name: loop
tests.statement: A code with adj(0,0) is not in graphClass; one with adj(0,1) and not adj(1,0) is not.

tests.name: one_edge_orbit
tests.statement: The codes of the one-edge graphs on {0,1} and {5,7} are isomorphic; the one-edge graph and the two-edge path are not.

tests.name: clopen_conditions
tests.statement: Membership depends only on the values at adjAtom i i, adjAtom i j and adjAtom j i: an intersection of clopen sets (isClopen_setOf_eval).

targets.name: borelComplete_graphClass
targets.statement: BorelComplete graphClass, witnessed for each L' by one continuous map RelationalConfiguration L' ℕ → RelationalConfiguration Language.graph ℕ (relabelled tagged incidence graph) that lands in graphClass and reflects and preserves isomorphism. The code of the tagged incidence graph is SimpleGraph.toRelationalConfiguration, relabelled to ℕ; it lands in graphClass by IsSimpleGraph.restrict.

locator.where: Theorem 1; statement also at camerlo-gao-boolean lines 111–112 and paolini-shelah-tfab line 125

targets.name: ratColour
targets.statement: ν : ℚ → ℕ, ν r = padicValNat 2 r.den; each fibre ν⁻¹(m) is dense in ℚ and the fibres partition ℚ.

locator.where: Lemma VI.18, lines 4258–4260 (maps onto children with dense preimages)

api.name: dense_ratColour_preimage
api.statement: For every m, ν⁻¹(m) is dense in ℚ.

api.name: ratColour_eq_iff
